## What it does — the source's own header, verbatim

```
retire_commentary.c — restores the cut player-retirement commentary
  PWS_RETIRE04 (eid 119), PWS_RETIRE01 (eid 118), PWS_RETIRE02 (eid 117)

WHY THIS EXISTS
  The game ships a working emitter (sub_41B250) for these three lines, but it
  is only reached from sub_4F1FE0's FinishState == 0 arm behind conditions that
  never come true for a human driver. Four designed live runs on 2026-07-28
  proved it is unreachable by gameplay: it is NOT the dword_7CE814 gate (that
  reads 0 naturally in-race), NOT a timer race (an 11.0 s window was measured
  against a 10.0 s dwell), and NOT the dwell itself (30 s stationary with every
  precondition satisfied still produced nothing). See findings.jsonl.

  The clips, their score mapping and the audio path are all intact — a direct
  queue injection of eid 117 was confirmed audible by ear in the same session.
  So this DLL does not fix the emitter; it watches for the retirement the game
  itself performs and injects the matching event.

WHAT IT DOES
  Polls the player vehicle. When FinishState (veh+0x4064) transitions to 2
  (the game's own "retired" value), it reads ReasonCode (veh+0x4068) and
  injects the line the emitter would have chosen:
      ReasonCode 1 -> eid 119   (PWS_RETIRE04)
      ReasonCode 7 -> eid 118   (PWS_RETIRE01)
      otherwise    -> eid 117   (PWS_RETIRE02)
  That branch mapping is read straight out of sub_41B250, not invented.

  No code hook, no trampoline, no byte patch — a polling thread only. Nothing
  is written except the commentary queue, which is the same write path already
  proven in mods/grid_reorder/gr21.c.

BUILD
  C:\msys64\mingw32\bin\gcc.exe -shared -O2 -o retire_commentary.dll retire_commentary.c -lkernel32

TRUST
  All addresses below are FACT/CONFIRMED in name_index.json / findings.jsonl.
  Exe is non-ASLR (image base 0x400000) so absolute addresses are literal.
```
